const-p-1417-2025-d-b-rahmatullah-anothe.excerpt: SCUG employees, not being civil servants, may invoke Article 199 against a transfer, but that settles only the forum: no one has a vested right to a particular station, and interference lies solely for breach of statutor
const-p-1417-2025-d-b-rahmatullah-anothe.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
const-p-1417-2025-d-b-rahmatullah-anothe.full_text:
Const. P. 1417/2025 (D.B.) Rahmatullah & Another V/S P.O Sindh & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

SCUG employees, not being civil servants, may invoke Article 199 against a transfer, but that settles only the forum: no one has a vested right to a particular station, and interference lies solely for breach of statutory tenure or rule, or mala fides on the record. Refusal of the main relief, however, does not bar a direction to the authority to post the employee to a post that lawfully exists.

2026-shc-suk-1894.title: Const. P. 144/2023 (S.B.) Mst. Amna Shaikh V/S Imran Ahmed Shaikh & another
2026-shc-suk-1894.excerpt: A Nikahnama entry showing dower as prompt proves the obligation, not its payment. Section 10(4) of the Act of 1964 allows restoration only of dower actually received, and its relinquishment is itself the Zar-e-Khula. The
2026-shc-suk-1894.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1894.full_text:
Const. P. 144/2023 (S.B.) Mst. Amna Shaikh V/S Imran Ahmed Shaikh & another
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A Nikahnama entry showing dower as prompt proves the obligation, not its payment. Section 10(4) of the Act of 1964 allows restoration only of dower actually received, and its relinquishment is itself the Zar-e-Khula. The Qanun-e-Shahadat being excluded by section 17, a wife's consistent account of an ordinary dowry list proves it and cannot be reduced by the Court's own estimate of her family's means.

2026-shc-suk-1915.title: Const. P. 203/2026 (D.B.) Hyder Shaikh V/S P.O Sindh & Others
2026-shc-suk-1915.excerpt: An employee of a Local Council, though a public servant under Section 151 of the Act of 2013, is not a civil servant; but Rule 26 of the Rules of 2017 carried the benefit of Rule 11-A to him mutatis mutandis until 18.10.
2026-shc-suk-1915.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
2026-shc-suk-1915.full_text:
Const. P. 203/2026 (D.B.) Hyder Shaikh V/S P.O Sindh & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

An employee of a Local Council, though a public servant under Section 151 of the Act of 2013, is not a civil servant; but Rule 26 of the Rules of 2017 carried the benefit of Rule 11-A to him mutatis mutandis until 18.10.2024. After Muhammad Jalal, no fresh entitlement survives; a right accrued on a death before that date stands preserved alike for both classes, with limitation running from majority where the dependant was a minor.

2026-shc-suk-1914.excerpt: The amenability of a public-sector company to Article 199 is not the same as the justiciability of the right asserted. Where service is governed by non-statutory policy, the relationship is that of master and servant, an
2026-shc-suk-1914.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
2026-shc-suk-1914.full_text:
Const. P. 1231/2021 (D.B.) Sattar Bux Soomro & Others V/S Federation of Pakistan & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

The amenability of a public-sector company to Article 199 is not the same as the justiciability of the right asserted. Where service is governed by non-statutory policy, the relationship is that of master and servant, and the claim lies before a court of plenary jurisdiction, recasting such a money claim as discrimination under Article 25 cannot unlock a jurisdiction otherwise barred.

2026-shc-suk-1913.title: R.A (Civil Revision) 173/2023 (S.B.) Late Alllah Dino Through his LRs V/S Muhammad Zafar & Others
2026-shc-suk-1913.excerpt: A registered thirty-year-old deed is presumed genuine under Articles 85(5), 100 and 129(e) QSO, 1984. The burden shifts to its beneficiary only once the challenger goes beyond bare denial. Its cancellation is governed by
2026-shc-suk-1913.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1913.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 173/2023 (S.B.) Late Alllah Dino Through his LRs V/S Muhammad Zafar & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A registered thirty-year-old deed is presumed genuine under Articles 85(5), 100 and 129(e) QSO, 1984. The burden shifts to its beneficiary only once the challenger goes beyond bare denial. Its cancellation is governed by Article 91 of the Limitation Act, and forgery gives no immunity from time. A reversing decree that ignores those presumptions, awards possession and mesne profits without findings, and binds co-heirs never impleaded cannot stand. Non-joinder calls for impleadment, not dismissal.

2026-shc-suk-1912.title: R.A (Civil Revision) 192/2018 (S.B.) Muhammad Tagial Maitlo V/S Wazeer Ali & Others
2026-shc-suk-1912.excerpt: An oral sale agreement, unproved for want of particulars and independent evidence, gives no right to cancel a registered deed, section 39 aside, because it creates no interest in land. A co-defendant's admission through
2026-shc-suk-1912.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1912.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 192/2018 (S.B.) Muhammad Tagial Maitlo V/S Wazeer Ali & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

An oral sale agreement, unproved for want of particulars and independent evidence, gives no right to cancel a registered deed, section 39 aside, because it creates no interest in land. A co-defendant's admission through an attorney who never deposed cannot displace the deed's presumption. The purchaser for value in good faith is protected by section 27(b) unless notice is brought home to him.

2026-shc-suk-1927.excerpt: Entrustment is the foundation of Section 409 PPC and a shortage cannot be proved by figures consolidated in office while the primary record is withheld though available. A book shortage apportioned between two officials,
2026-shc-suk-1927.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1927.full_text:
Criminal Appeal 87/2023 (S.B.) Iqbal Hussain Jumani V/S The State
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Entrustment is the foundation of Section 409 PPC and a shortage cannot be proved by figures consolidated in office while the primary record is withheld though available. A book shortage apportioned between two officials, one neither tried nor examined, is no proof of dishonest conversion.

2026-shc-suk-1924.title: R.A (Civil Revision) 186/2011 (S.B.) Muhammad Ramzan V/S Chandarban and other
2026-shc-suk-1924.excerpt: In a suit under Section 8 of the Act of 1877, the manner of dispossession is no ingredient of relief, where title stands proved, the case turns on the identity of the plot on the ground, which the court may settle by a l
2026-shc-suk-1924.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1924.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 186/2011 (S.B.) Muhammad Ramzan V/S Chandarban and other
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

In a suit under Section 8 of the Act of 1877, the manner of dispossession is no ingredient of relief, where title stands proved, the case turns on the identity of the plot on the ground, which the court may settle by a local investigation of its own motion under Section 75 read with Order XXVI Rule 9 CPC. A decree for possession of a plot left unidentified, with the commission ordered after judgment, is not executable and both decrees being so flawed, remand follows.

2026-shc-suk-1925.title: R.A (Civil Revision) 31/2016 (S.B.) Mohammad Ishaque Kamboh V/S Mohammad Ameen and others
2026-shc-suk-1925.excerpt: A Revenue Officer who, under the guise of correcting the record, adjudicates a stranger's title acts beyond his power and an order so made against a man long dead and without notice to his recorded heirs is a nullity tha
2026-shc-suk-1925.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1925.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 31/2016 (S.B.) Mohammad Ishaque Kamboh V/S Mohammad Ameen and others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A Revenue Officer who, under the guise of correcting the record, adjudicates a stranger's title acts beyond his power and an order so made against a man long dead and without notice to his recorded heirs is a nullity that section 172 does not protect. An entry confers no title, he who claims through it must prove the transaction behind it.

2026-shc-suk-1926.title: Criminal Appeal 88/2023 (S.B.) Iqbal Hussain Jumani V/S The State
2026-shc-suk-1926.excerpt: Entrustment proved and the stock short, the cause lies especially within the accused's knowledge and a deficiency unexplained and unrecouped spells dishonest conversion. Payment after challan discharges only the civil li
2026-shc-suk-1926.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-suk-1926.full_text:
Criminal Appeal 88/2023 (S.B.) Iqbal Hussain Jumani V/S The State
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Entrustment proved and the stock short, the cause lies especially within the accused's knowledge and a deficiency unexplained and unrecouped spells dishonest conversion. Payment after challan discharges only the civil liability; a No Dues Certificate is a receipt, not an acquittal and departmental recovery with penalty is no double jeopardy.

2026-shc-lar-1941.title: Const. P. 326/2026 (D.B.) Irshad Khatoon V/S The P.O Sindh & others
2026-shc-lar-1941.excerpt: Every limb of section 2(f) of the Act of 2014, as it stood in 2015, is tied to terrorism, and a constable killed by negligent driving, though on duty, falls outside it; the substitution of 2023 enlarges the class of bene
2026-shc-lar-1941.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi
2026-shc-lar-1941.full_text:
Const. P. 326/2026 (D.B.) Irshad Khatoon V/S The P.O Sindh & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

Every limb of section 2(f) of the Act of 2014, as it stood in 2015, is tied to terrorism, and a constable killed by negligent driving, though on duty, falls outside it; the substitution of 2023 enlarges the class of beneficiaries, is substantive and prospective, and its "act of violence" imports intentional force. Entitlement crystallises on the date of death, and declarations wrongly made in other cases found no claim, Article 25 knowing no negative equality.

Where the department's own record is self-contradictory, the candidate is sent back for a reasoned decision, not non-suited.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri(Author)

Mere disagreement with the appreciation of evidence or the conclusions reached by the Courts below does not furnish a ground for interference under Article 199 of the Constitution. The Honourable Supreme Court has consistently emphasized that the legislative scheme governing family disputes must be respected and that constitutional jurisdiction cannot be invoked to circumvent the statutory restriction on further appeals. Consequently, the petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed in limine

const-p-6736-2026-d-b-altaf-karim-others.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri(Author)
const-p-6736-2026-d-b-altaf-karim-others.full_text:
Const. P. 6736/2026 (D.B.) Altaf Karim & others V/S Idrees Sattar Agar & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Saleem Jessar, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Abdul Hamid Bhurgri(Author)

It is well settled that availability of an alternate remedy does not constitute an absolute bar to constitutional jurisdiction; nevertheless, where an adequate and efficacious remedy exists before the competent forum, constitutional jurisdiction is not ordinarily exercised unless exceptional circumstances, such as patent want of jurisdiction, manifest illegality or infringement of a fundamental right incapable of adequate redress through the ordinary remedy, are demonstrated. No such exceptional circumstance has been shown in the present case. Consequently, the Constitution Petition, being misconceived in the present form, is dismissed in limine.

Cr.Bail 501/2026 (S.B.) Ghulam Fareed Jakhrani and Others V/S The State
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Where the FIR describes the assailants as strangers to be identified on sight, their nomination eleven days later, through identical statements of related witnesses, without an identification parade, is weak evidence and brings the case within section 497(2) Cr.P.C. The recovery of commonplace articles, unsupported by any forensic link, furnishes no corroboration. For pre-arrest bail, the record of a failed earlier prosecution over the same land and a role of armed presence alone supply the inference of mala fide.

2026-shc-lar-1996.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
2026-shc-lar-1996.full_text:
Criminal Miscelleneous 335/2026 (S.B.) Rasheed Khan & Others V/S PO Sindh & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A Magistrate acting on a report under section 173 Cr.P.C is not a criminal court, so no revision lies, even if section 561-A applies to an abuse of process. He must apply his own mind to cognisance, and if the offences are exclusively triable by a Special Judge, record reasons, decline cognizance, and return the report. He may neither choose the investigating agency nor direct how it shall proceed, and custody of an accused passes only by order of a competent court.

Service under a corporation is not service under Government, and absorption into a Government post carries past service across only if the instrument of absorption so provides. Admittedly, the Petitioner contested the suit in full before the Family Court by filing his written statement and evidence and appearing as a witness and the decree was passed on merits after hearing both sides. The Petitioner???s application under Section 12(2) CPC did not identify any fraud, misrepresentation or concealment of the kind the provision requires and the Family Court rightly dismissed it. Further, the Section 14 of the Family Courts Act, 1964 prescribes a strict limitation period for appeals. A party seeking condonation under Section 5 of the Limitation Act must explain each day of delay with sufficient cause. A bare assertion that the previous counsel did not disclose the limitation period is not sufficient cause. Such a plea, by itself, does not automatically entitle a litigant to condonation, which remains subject to the applicable law and the facts and circumstances of the case. The Appellate Court???s order dismissing the application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act and the time-barred appeal is therefore well within the law. It discloses no illegality, jurisdictional defect, misreading or non-reading of evidence, or other infirmity warranting interference by this Court in its constitutional jurisdiction. The Petitioner has attempted through successive proceedings to reopen a decree that was passed on merits after full contest. Accordingly, the petition is without merit and is dismissed in limine, along with pending application(s), if any.

As no Special Court has been established under the Act of 2024, only the District and Sessions Judge, as the competent court under section 2(qq), may deal with such a trial; an order of an Additional Sessions Judge is without jurisdiction and void. As the appeal under section 32 lies only against a Special Court???s order, an interlocutory order under section 516-A Cr.P.C. is examinable in revision, and the appeal may be converted ex debito justitiae.

2026-shc-khi-2100.title: Const. P. 847/2025 (S.B.) Muhammad Hanif Ansari V/S Muhammad Haseeb Ansari & Others
2026-shc-khi-2100.excerpt: 18. In the present case, the petitioner has failed to demonstrate that the learned trial Court or either of the revisional Courts exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction vested by law, or
2026-shc-khi-2100.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Zulfiqar Ali Sangi(Author)
2026-shc-khi-2100.full_text:
Const. P. 847/2025 (S.B.) Muhammad Hanif Ansari V/S Muhammad Haseeb Ansari & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Zulfiqar Ali Sangi(Author)

18. In the present case, the petitioner has failed to demonstrate that the learned trial Court or either of the revisional Courts exercised jurisdiction not vested in it, failed to exercise jurisdiction vested by law, or acted in a manner resulting in a patent illegality requiring correction under Article 199 of the Constitution. The impugned orders disclose consideration of the earlier litigation, the relevant documents, the timing of the transfer and the legal provisions relied upon by the parties. The petitioner's disagreement with the conclusions reached by the Courts below does not furnish sufficient justification for this Court to reopen the matter in its constitutional jurisdiction. For the foregoing reasons, this Court finds that the petitioner has failed to make out a case for interference with the order dated 20.08.2020, as maintained by the learned Vth Additional District Judge, Karachi West, through order dated 22.01.2022, or with the order dated 14.01.2023, as maintained by the learned IXth Additional District Judge, Karachi West, through order dated 29.11.2023. No sufficient jurisdictional defect, patent illegality or material irregularity has been established to warrant setting aside the impugned orders. 19. Accordingly, the instant constitutional petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed. The impugned orders dated 20.08.2020, 22.01.2022, 14.01.2023 and 29.11.2023 are maintained. There shall be no order as to costs.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

Safe custody is proved by producing every hand that held the parcel with its contemporaneous entry, and a difference over who carried the already sealed parcels on a short joint journey leaves no gap in the chain. Where a portion is drawn and tested from each slab separately, the whole quantity is proved, and a conviction recorded under the wrong clause of the Table, the accused having been charged and tried under the right one, is a curable slip.

Amenity land can be used for no other purpose, and any grant of it is void, but only once the plot is shown to be amenity land; absent any plan or notification, and with rival entries held by strangers to the record, title is a disputed fact for the Tribunal. Article 199 yields no more than a direction to decide the pending application by a speaking order after notice to every claimant.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

The Tribunal alone decides whether land is public property, and a private person may move it where officials do not act. Having accepted a demarcation report that part of the land belongs to the village, it could not dismiss the suit without framing issues or recording evidence; the remedy is remand, not a declaration of encroachment by this Court.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

A member of the Sindh Councils Unified Grades is not a civil servant, and his service rests on statutory rules. Article 199 applies. Only the Government may move him between Councils, so a Chairman???s relieving letter effects nothing. Where the arrears turn on records the authority itself holds, the Court directs it to verify, hear and decide rather than decree or dismiss.

12. It is clarified that the findings of the learned appellate Court regarding entitlement of the minor to maintenance and the quantum thereof shall remain undisturbed. Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Faisal Kamal Alam, Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana(Author)

Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 - Shrine bombing (4 killed, 16 injured) - Eyewitness identification found reliable despite absence of formal identification parade, corroborated by medical and technical evidence - Plea of false implication unsupported - Khalil Ahmed specifically identified as carrying and placing the explosive device; conviction and death sentence maintained - Abdul Rehman identified as accompanying him, without any specific act of placing or activating the device attributed to him - Conviction maintained, but lesser role treated as mitigating circumstance warranting commutation of death sentence to imprisonment for life - Khalil Ahmed???s appeal dismissed; Abdul Rehman???s appeal partly allowed to the extent of sentence - Murder Reference answered accordingly.

2026-shc-suk-2139.full_text:

Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997- Imam Bargah suicide bombing (63 killed, 73 injured)- Convictions maintained -Reliable identification by injured eyewitness - Absence of formal identification parade not fatal in the circumstances - Omission under Section 342, Cr.P.C., not fatal in the absence of prejudice - Recovery of concealed explosives at appellants??? pointation - Custodial disclosure admissible only to the extent of discovery under Article 40, Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 - Non-association of private mashirs not fatal where recovery evidence is trustworthy - Conscious possession of explosives established - Presumption under Section 27-A, ATA, attracted - Appeals dismissed.

2026-shc-lar-2144.full_text:
R.A (Civil Revision) 9/2006 (S.B.) Muhammad Bachal V/S Khawand Dino and others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

The Board of Revenue has no power of suo motu review: an order reopening its own final decision on the Colonization Officer???s report, without an application by an aggrieved person and beyond time, is without lawful authority. Notice and hearing supply no power the law withholds, and the ouster of civil jurisdiction does not protect it. A revision out of time does not oust the Court???s suo motu power under section 115 CPC where such a jurisdictional error appears.

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Where two public bodies hold rival claims over the suit land, the body whose allotment and entries are in question is, at least, a proper party, and no decree can bind it in its absence. An application under Order I, Rule 10(2), C.P.C., cannot be decided against the plaint as it stands. Sub-rule (4) provides for amendment nor against the Plaintiff???s own title and the Court may add a party of its own motion. Delay apart, interference lies where the Court below applies the wrong test.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

At preliminary enquiry stage, Court is only to ascertain whether sufficient grounds exist for proceeding and cannot conduct a meticulous appraisal or determine the complaint on merits. Where police officials are accused of custodial / encounter killing, enquiry by officer of the same police force defeat the object of an impartial enquiry. Police cannot be investigator of their own cause. Dismissal of Direct Complaint set aside and matter remanded for fresh enquiry.

Bench: Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Suresh Kumar

Recovery of 5,010 grams of charas in six separate pieces-Sample drawn from only one piece and found positive for charas- No separate sampling and chemical examination of the remaining pieces - Principle laid down in Ameer Zeb v. Const. P. 640/2026 (D.B.) Muhammad Hassan Lohar V/S Province of Sindh & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

Conditional offer letter, neither accepted nor acted upon, does not created vested right or enforceable right. Where the genuineness of the recruitment process and offer letter involves seriously disputed questions of fact, constitutional jurisdiction cannot be invoked to establish such a right; however, candidates cannot be non-suited outright where the issuance of the offer letter is affirmed by the officers who signed them. Independent departmental verification of the original recruitment record directed.

ii-a-12-2026-s-b-rasool-bux-and-others-v.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

State land under running harap grant. Agreement to sale does not create any right, title or interest in the immovable property; where property rights have not yet been conferred upon the grantee. Such agreement is at best contingent and becomes enforceable only upon conferment of those rights. Mere occupation of State land without grant creates no right against the lawful allottee. Second Appeal dismissed.

2026-shc-khi-2166.full_text:
M.A. 112/2025 (S.B.) Salman Masud V/S Institute of Chartered Accounts of Pakistan (ICAP)
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Justice Ms. Sana Akram Minhas(Author)

Chartered Accountants Ordinance, 1961 - Disciplinary proceedings and imposition of penalty by Institute of Chartered Accountants of Pakistan (ICAP) - Failure to record reasons justifying imposition of severest category of penalty - Non-consideration of mitigating circumstances - Proportionality of sanction to be assessed with reference to misconduct actually established and not on the entire range of allegations originally levelled - One-year removal from Register of Members held disproportionate - High Court sets aside penalty and imposes formal reprimand.

spl-cr-j-a-140-2016-d-b-siraj-khan-arain.full_text:
Spl.Cr.J.A 140/2016 (D.B.) Siraj Khan Arain V/S The State
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Faisal Kamal Alam(Author), Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana

Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997, S.9(c): Safe custody and safe transmission of samples (480 kg charas) not proved: benefit of doubt. Register No. XIX entry not produced, and neither the Malkhana Incharge nor the carrier constable was examined. A positive Chemical Examiner???s report cannot cure the break in the chain of custody (2025 SCMR 923). Appeal allowed; acquitted.

spl-cr-j-a-214-2016-d-b-islam-shaikh-v-s.title: Spl.Cr.J.A 214/2016 (D.B.) Islam Shaikh V/S The State
spl-cr-j-a-214-2016-d-b-islam-shaikh-v-s.excerpt: Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997, S.9(c): Safe custody and safe transmission of the charas (40 kg), not established: benefit of doubt. The prosecution did not produce the Malkhana Register No. XIX entry, did not
spl-cr-j-a-214-2016-d-b-islam-shaikh-v-s.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Faisal Kamal Alam(Author), Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana
spl-cr-j-a-214-2016-d-b-islam-shaikh-v-s.full_text:
Spl.Cr.J.A 214/2016 (D.B.) Islam Shaikh V/S The State
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Faisal Kamal Alam(Author), Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana

Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997, S.9(c): Safe custody and safe transmission of the charas (40 kg), not established: benefit of doubt. The prosecution did not produce the Malkhana Register No. XIX entry, did not examine the Malkhana Incharge, and did not examine the Excise Constable through whom the property was sent to the Chemical Examiner. The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 also differed on who held the charas and on the sequence of sealing. A break in the chain of custody is not cured by a positive Chemical Examiner???s report recording intact seals, and the conviction (life imprisonment) was set aside. Appeal allowed; appellant acquitted.

cr-rev-58-2023-d-b-asadullah-v-s-the-sta.judges: Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Suresh Kumar
cr-rev-58-2023-d-b-asadullah-v-s-the-sta.full_text:
Cr.Rev 58/2023 (D.B.) Asadullah V/S The State & others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Suresh Kumar

**Tagline:** Criminal Revision for enhancement of sentence from life imprisonment to death under ss. 302(b)/149 PPC dismissed. Enhancement is an exceptional power, exercised only on gross misreading of evidence or grave miscarriage of justice; proof of the charge alone does not require death. As the roles of the nine respondents were not identical and the injuries were caused by butts and blunt weapons, life imprisonment was not manifestly inadequate. Pending appeal against conviction (Crl. Appeal No.S-76 of 2023) to be decided on its own merits, uninfluenced by this order.

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A plaintiff claiming derivative title must prove the title of his predecessor and succeed on the strength of his own case; revenue entries do not, by themselves, create title. Instruments neither produced nor proved in evidence cannot be cancelled, particularly in the absence of necessary parties whose rights would be affected.

const-p-222-2026-s-b-nazir-ahmed-others-.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)
const-p-222-2026-s-b-nazir-ahmed-others-.full_text:
Const. P. 222/2026 (S.B.) Nazir Ahmed & others V/S PO Sindh & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

A plaint cannot be rejected under Order VII Rule 11, C.P.C., on the basis of limitation, locus standi, or fraud, where disputed facts and defence material are in issue. The plaint is read as a whole; its averments are taken as true, and mixed questions of law and fact must go to trial. A revisional court under Section 115 that reverses a trial court???s correct refusal to reject the plaint, after issues are framed and evidence has begun, exercises jurisdiction not vested in it. Such a revisional order, though a decree, is neither appealable under Section 96 nor open to second revision (Section 115(3)), and is challengeable under Article 199 constitution of Pakistan, 1973.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author)

Order XXIII Rule 1, C.P.C. Permission to withdraw a suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit can be granted only upon a formal defect or other sufficient ground duly recorded by the Court. Where such permission is refused or subsequently set aside, a conditional request for withdrawal cannot be converted into withdrawal simpliciter, as the plaintiff must retain the choice to continue with the original suit rather than suffer the bar against a fresh action. Original suit restored.

Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arbab Ali Hakro(Author), Hon'ble Mr. Justice Muhammad Osman Ali Hadi

An Enquiry Officer appointed under the Sindh Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 may inquire into tampering with revenue records and determine the responsibility of the officials concerned, but this authority does not extend to deciding ownership of immovable property or directing the cancellation or substitution of revenue entries. Determination of disputed title lies with the competent forum under the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 or, where appropriate, the civil court.

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Omar Sial(Author)

The court emphasized that attempted sexual abuse of a minor is a grave offense, warranting denial of bail despite the defense's claims of lack of sodomy. The court rejected the argument that the case was fabricated, citing the boy's credible testimony and the potential for severe punishment under relevant sections. The decision underscores the seriousness of such offenses and the court's duty to protect societal interests by denying bail until the trial concludes.

2026-shc-khi-2328.judges: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arshad Hussain Khan, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Amjad Ali Sahito(Author)
2026-shc-khi-2328.full_text:
H.C.A 364/2006 (D.B.) Younus Billoo V/S Mst. Piyari Begum
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Arshad Hussain Khan, Hon'ble Mr. Justice Amjad Ali Sahito(Author)

Time is not the essence of a sale agreement for immovable property unless clearly stated, and specific performance may be granted if the parties are ready and willing to perform. The court emphasized that time is not the essence of a sale agreement for immovable property unless clearly stated. The appellant's readiness and willingness to perform, evidenced by payments and deposit of the balance, justified specific performance. The court rejected the respondent's claims of cancellation and enhancement, upheld the sale agreement, and directed the respondents to execute the sale deed within 60 days, with the deposited amount released upon completion.

succession-appeal-2-2024-s-b-mst-raheema.full_text:
Succession Appeal 2/2024 (S.B.) Mst. Raheema Through Attorney V/S Mst. Umme-Farwah & Others
Sindh High Court

Bench: Hon'ble Justice Ms. Tasneem Sultana(Author)

Sindh Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021, Ss. 2(b), 5(b) & 10: Where a genuine controversy requiring adjudication has already arisen before the Court, referral to NADRA for a formal decline would serve no purpose. Gratuity and family pension are governed by the West Pakistan Civil Services Pension Rules (Rr. 4.7, 4.8, 4.10) and do not form part of the estate. The mother has no concurrent share in them where the deceased leaves a widow and children, and the deceased's acknowledgment of his daughters in earlier judicial proceedings outweighs conflicting registration entries.
